notes: TRIAL catalog authored 2026-11-11 for the 64 m x 64 m Jornada-style grass/shrub example case. Two species, ONE complete record each (all traits of a species stay together). Biomass everywhere is kg DRY aboveground mass (no roots, no tissue water). Root layers are the three SYRUP soil layers [0,0.2], [0.2,0.5], [0.5,1.2] m (shallow to deep; see soil.toml in the case root). Provenance tags used in notes/status: [USER] user request; [AUTHOR] author trial choice, not calibrated; [DERIVED] arithmetic from tagged inputs; [LIT] published value used as stated; [EXAMPLE] copied from an existing LEAF example fixture; [PROXY] proxy-species or conditional source. Exact per-parameter provenance and citations: PARAMETERS.md and SOURCES.md in the case root (this file is also in the case root). REVISION literature_parameters_20261111 rev1: NO numeric trait value was changed (no source was found whose quantity maps defensibly onto a native trait definition); only provenance/status text, the references lists and this catalog_id changed. Literature added as constraints/consistency checks (full per-row links and units: PARAMETERS.md, research_notes.md in the task directory): Steinberg 2001 FEIS https://research.fs.usda.gov/feis/species-reviews/progla ; Simonin 2000 FEIS https://research.fs.usda.gov/feis/species-reviews/boueri ; Hanson 1982 J. Range Manage. 35(4):455-458 (https://rangelandsgateway.org/dlio/22027); Valentine 1970 NMSU Bull. 553 and Nelson 1934 USDA Tech. Bull. 409 and Neilson 1986 Science 232:27-34 (all via FEIS); Peters 2002 Am. J. Bot. 89:1616 https://doi.org/10.3732/ajb.89.10.1616 (abstract only); Golubov et al. 1999 J. Ecol. 87:955 ; Ansley et al. 2010 GCB Bioenergy 2:26-36 ; Ludwig et al. 1975 Am. Midl. Nat. 94:451-461 (only a secondary summary was read). STEPWAT2 pinned 003cb9b4 inputs (testing.sagebrush.master) are sagebrush-steppe resource groups with no black grama or mesquite record and no number was adopted from them. The saved preview population was initialised with the FROZEN earlier catalog preview/species_at_initialization.json (catalog_id jornada_grass05_shrub10_trial_20261111, allometry/ages unchanged), so this active catalog has a different catalog hash and a new initialization is required before any new run (not run). NOTHING in this file is a field calibration or a validation of Jornada vegetation dynamics. Strict native keys only: unknown keys are refused by the LEAF loaders, so commentary lives in notes/status/units/references fields.

BOER.name: black grama proxy (Bouteloua eriopoda), trial parameters
BOER.notes: Black grama proxy. Initial population (cover 0.05, diameter mean 0.10 m, SD 0.02 m) is a [USER] choice in generation.json (case root), not a measured field estimate. Allometry, growth, water-use, mortality, disturbance and reproduction numbers are [AUTHOR] trial hypotheses unless a section note says [LIT]/[DERIVED]/[EXAMPLE]. USDA FEIS (Simonin 2000) supports qualitative statements only (long-lived warm-season C4 bunchgrass, upper-soil root concentration with roots to about 1.2 m, summer growth, vegetative spread) and does not supply any exact coefficient below.

allometry.notes: [EXAMPLE]+[AUTHOR] diameter exponent 0.45 and a=0.9 follow the LEAF example fixture grass diameter law; the height law a=0.9,b=0.3 is an [AUTHOR] trial anchor. Neither is a published standing-biomass equation and ANPP regressions must not be substituted. [DERIVED] mean diameter 0.10 m implies B = (0.10/0.9)**(1/0.45) = 0.0075763685 kg dry AGB and height about 0.208 m (FEIS only supports plausibility of tens-of-cm stems).

roots.notes: lateral_radius_multiplier 3.0 = lower endpoint of the [USER] 3-5 x canopy-radius range (grass endpoint is an [AUTHOR] trial choice). layer_fractions [DERIVED] from the [LIT] Vito&Sala 2026 black grama combined-years tracer-uptake fit F(z)=1-beta**z (z in CENTIMETRES, beta=0.977) integrated over layer edges 0,20,50,120 cm: fraction=(beta**lo-beta**hi)/(1-beta**120); the conditional normalisation over the modelled 1.2 m omits a tail of 0.0612840765 of the fitted curve. Tracer absorption is an uptake proxy, not measured root density; fixed profile, no plasticity. Every layer is reached. HORIZONTAL law (current shared root builder): uniform weight per cell POSITIVELY overlapped by the root disk (including barely touched cells), clipped to the finite domain; NOT overlap-area weighting and NOT a measured radial root-density law; it multiplies these per-species vertical fractions. On CUDA daily demand/withdrawal run on-device, but the weekly geometry/root rebuild is host/compiled with explicit CSR uploads (not fully GPU-resident).

porosity.status: uncalibrated constant copied from the existing LEAF example fixture [EXAMPLE]; unused by LEAF ecology but consumed by native MAPLE wind

growth.status: AUTHOR trial hypotheses within the native admitted ranges (rate 0..1 per year); STEPWAT2 (Palmquist 2018) is a structural precedent only and no STEP number is adopted; NOT a fit to the 295 per year Setaria diagnostic.

units.biomass_support_kg_year_per_m3: kg dry AGB supported per m3 of water, in kg*year/m3 [DERIVED] k = live_fraction/(365*q) at reference PET, q=0.0234 m3/kg/day: a support-balance prior, NOT a production yield or WUE
units.live_fraction: fraction of AGB that is live/transpiring [AUTHOR]
units.monthly_activity: fraction 0..1, January..December [ASSUMED SHAPE, not a measured coefficient], constrained only by FEIS (Simonin 2000, https://research.fs.usda.gov/feis/species-reviews/boueri, Chihuahuan Desert phenology) qualitative dates: growth begins late April-early May, flowering late Aug-early Sep, fruiting late Sep-early Oct; Jornada growth periods 0-176 days per year (1925-1935) set by rainfall, so a fixed calendar curve is a prior
units.temperature_min_c: degC cardinal minimum [ASSUMED prior; no black grama measurement found]
units.temperature_opt_c: degC cardinal optimum [ASSUMED prior; no black grama measurement found; C4 warm-season qualitative only]
units.temperature_max_c: degC cardinal maximum [ASSUMED prior; no black grama measurement found]

growth.notes: Literature check rev1: mature_biomass_kg, intrinsic_rate_per_year, live_fraction and extra_growth_rate_per_year remain [AUTHOR] hypotheses: no per-plant standing dry aboveground biomass saturation, live fraction or annual rate for black grama could be read from an accessible primary source (Jornada archive PDFs were unreachable: DNS failure); FEIS reports only forage production/regrowth qualitatively. Temperature multiplier gates demand and growth; there is NO freezing-mortality or fire module in the model. The growth fraction U/D is applied once, in total across roots; unmet demand is not relocated. Water is owned and debited by SYRUP exactly once. Annual calendar normalization follows the native code.

water_use.status: demand coefficient [PROXY] from a local descriptive reanalysis of moist-soil savanna grasses (Belovitch 2023 released data); reference PET [AUTHOR].

units.demand_m3_per_kg_day: m3 per kg of STANDING DRY AGB per day (23.4 L/kg/day, moist-bin median of 30 individual means, harvest mass not daily mass; not a printed universal coefficient)
units.reference_pet_mm_per_day: mm/day normalisation chosen by the AUTHOR; not a measured experimental or site mean PET

water_use.notes: Demand D = B * demand * (PET/reference_pet) * dt * activity * temperature_factor, applied per total dry AGB. Scaling by PET ratio, monthly activity and temperature is LEAF's chosen adaptation, not a source-calibrated equation. Not a Jornada adult black grama measurement.

reproduction.status: AUTHOR trial numbers; qualitative precedent plus order-of-magnitude plausibility checks only. FEIS (Simonin 2000) cites Valentine 1970 (NMSU Bull. 553, deteriorated black grama range, 9-year grazing study, Chihuahuan Desert, NM): 2.1-2.8 stolons/plant and 0.19-0.31 ROOTED SETS/plant (grazing-intensity treatments; time basis per year not verified), Nelson 1934 (USDA Tech. Bull. 409): a favorable year is needed for stolon production and another for rooting, and Neilson 1986 (Science 232:27-34): seedlings in only 7 of 53 years. These are stolon/set counts and seedling-year frequencies, NOT a per-parent annual probability of a successful independent daughter, so probability 0.1, max_daughters 1 and every other number remain [AUTHOR] (0.1 daughters/parent/year is below the 0.19-0.31 sets/plant reading, i.e. not contradicted). Seed pathway stays null (Peters 2002 AJB 89:1616, abstract only: seed production/viability comparison, no establishment probability). Native reproduction requires a session reproduction_patch_size_m (5 m in case.toml, case root) only for species with a seed pathway.

units.probability: per eligible live parent and annual opportunity
units.initial_agb_dry_kg: kg dry aboveground per daughter, TRANSFERRED from the parent
units.dispersal_radius_m: m, uniform in a disk, finite non-periodic domain

reproduction.notes: Annual boundary is called once per year; daughters get new IDs and age 0 and are parent-funded. No seed bank, no water filter. Generation overlap=disallowed does not constrain later daughters.

life_expectancy.notes: [AUTHOR] nominal mean age-component lifespan, METADATA ONLY: it is not an age cutoff and no plant dies at this age. Literature check rev1: FEIS (Simonin 2000) citing Gould 1978 calls black grama 'long-lived' and, citing Nelson 1934, says established plants may persist 'several decades' through stoloniferous reproduction; that is a qualitative GENET persistence statement (ramets turn over), not a mean tussock/ramet lifespan, so 15 years is not changed or replaced by a maximum.

mortality.status: AUTHOR uncalibrated assumptions for every exact number; STEPWAT2 (Palmquist 2018) and ECOTONE (Peters 2002, https://doi.org/10.1016/S0304-3800(01)00460-4) are structural precedents only and do not supply these coefficients. background hazard is 0 to isolate the explicit age law.

units.biomass_loss_fraction: fraction of B lost by a surviving stressed plant [AUTHOR]

mortality.notes: Weibull mean = scale*Gamma(1+1/shape), so scale = 15/0.886226925 = 16.92568750643269. Full model lifespan can be shortened by stress and disturbance. No freezing mortality and no fire.

disturbance.status: ALL exact thresholds are AUTHOR testable response hypotheses, not literature coefficients. Abrasion is explicitly disabled (null) until a dose unit and calibrated response exist; sediment flux is never equated with dose. Establishment ground anchor is retained forever; evolving surface-to-soil remapping is deferred.

units.burial.lethal_height_fraction: fraction of plant height, absolute burial
units.exposure.injury_threshold_m: m of net erosion since the last evaluated state
units.max_injury_fraction: [0,1) fraction of dry AGB lost at saturation

disturbance.notes: Applied only after accepted wind/rain/recession transport diagnostics; never during growth.

PROGLA.name: honey mesquite proxy (Prosopis glandulosa), trial parameters
PROGLA.notes: Honey mesquite proxy. Initial population (cover 0.10, diameter mean 1.0 m, SD 0.10 m) is a [USER] choice in generation.json (case root), not a measured field estimate. Allometry, growth, mortality, disturbance and reproduction numbers are [AUTHOR] trial hypotheses unless tagged otherwise. USDA FEIS (Steinberg 2001) supports qualitative statements only (southwest deciduous seasonality, seed establishment, deep roots) and supplies no exact LEAF coefficient. The water-use coefficient is a conditional velvet-mesquite seedling/pot proxy, NOT an adult honey mesquite calibration.

allometry.notes: [EXAMPLE]+[AUTHOR] diameter law a=1.6,b=0.4 follows the LEAF example fixture shrub law; height a=0.8,b=0.4 gives H = D/2 exactly, matching the MAPLE reference shrub geometry (radius = height). Not a published standing-AGB equation. [DERIVED] mean diameter 1.0 m implies B = (1.0/1.6)**(1/0.4) = 0.3088161778 kg dry AGB and height 0.5 m.

roots.notes: lateral_radius_multiplier 5.0 = upper endpoint of the [USER] 3-5 x canopy-radius range (shrub endpoint is an [AUTHOR] trial choice). layer_fractions [DERIVED] from the [LIT] Vito&Sala 2026 honey mesquite combined-years tracer-uptake fit F(z)=1-beta**z (z in CENTIMETRES, beta=0.983) over layer edges 0,20,50,120 cm with conditional normalisation over 1.2 m (omitted tail 0.1277680127). This fitted-curve integration does not impose the paper's binned statement about uptake below 50 cm; do not confuse them. Tracer absorption is an uptake proxy, not root density; fixed profile; every layer is reached. HORIZONTAL law: uniform weight per cell positively overlapped by the root disk (including barely touched cells), clipped to the finite domain; not overlap-area weighting, not a measured radial density law; it multiplies these vertical fractions. On CUDA the weekly root rebuild is host/compiled with explicit CSR uploads (not fully GPU-resident).

porosity.status: uncalibrated constant copied from the existing LEAF example fixture [EXAMPLE]; unused by LEAF ecology but consumed by native MAPLE wind

growth.status: AUTHOR trial hypotheses within the native admitted ranges (rate 0..1 per year); STEPWAT2 (Palmquist 2018) is a structural precedent only; no STEP number is adopted.

units.biomass_support_kg_year_per_m3: kg*year/m3 [DERIVED] k = live_fraction/(365*q) at reference PET, q=0.0104 m3/kg/day: a support-balance prior, NOT a production yield or WUE
units.monthly_activity: fraction 0..1, January..December [ASSUMED SHAPE, not a measured coefficient], constrained by FEIS (Steinberg 2001, https://research.fs.usda.gov/feis/species-reviews/progla) western-Texas honey mesquite phenology table: dormant Nov-Mar, most beginning to leaf out 16 Apr, fully developed leaves 10 May, leaf drop generally Nov-Dec (often initiated by killing frost); these dates are Texas, not Jornada, observations
units.temperature_min_c: degC [ASSUMED prior; no honey mesquite measurement found for a minimum cardinal]
units.temperature_opt_c: degC [PROXY-CONSISTENT, shape ASSUMED] 30 equals the temperature of maximum net photosynthesis of the WEST-Texas honey mesquite population (20 degC for the east-Texas population), Hanson 1982 J. Range Manage. 35(4):455-458, https://rangelandsgateway.org/dlio/22027, controlled-environment seedling/plant measurements; a photosynthesis maximum is not a growth-rate cardinal optimum
units.temperature_max_c: degC [ASSUMED prior; Hanson 1982 reports lower net assimilation at 35 degC but no cardinal maximum was read]

growth.notes: Literature check rev1: mature_biomass_kg 10.0 kg remains an [AUTHOR] saturation cap; a secondary summary of Ludwig, Reynolds & Whitson 1975 (Am. Midl. Nat. 94:451-461, Chihuahuan Desert dry-weight dimension analysis) says Prosopis averaged over 10 kg aboveground, which is only order-of-magnitude supportive and was not read from the paper (a sample mean is not a saturation biomass). live_fraction 0.4 is not replaced: Ansley et al. 2010 (GCB Bioenergy 2:26-36, honey mesquite regrowth vs undisturbed trees; abstract/search summary only, site not verified) report leaf:twig mass near 1 and large stems >3 cm as 18% (7 yr) to 41% (12 yr) of regrowth tree mass, but the leaf+twig share of total standing dry mass of mature trees was not obtained and this does not map to the native live/transpiring fraction uniquely. Golubov et al. 1999 (J. Ecol. 87:955-962, honey mesquite, 1306 plants in 1 ha, 4 years, 9 size classes; site not verified from the abstract read) give lambda 1.29 for a population matrix, not a LEAF growth rate. Same shared rules as BOER: temperature gates demand/growth, no freeze mortality or fire, growth fraction applied once, water debited once by SYRUP.

water_use.status: demand coefficient [PROXY] = conditional velvet-mesquite (Prosopis velutina) seedling/pot value from Peterson & Neofotis 2004 (10.3-10.5 L/kg dry AGB/day; 10.4 chosen as the central proxy by the AUTHOR); reference PET [AUTHOR].

units.demand_m3_per_kg_day: m3 per kg of STANDING DRY AGB per day (10.4 L/kg/day; two seedlings in one pot treated as one virtual plant with AGB allocation assumptions; NOT adult honey mesquite)
units.reference_pet_mm_per_day: mm/day normalisation chosen by the AUTHOR; not a measured site mean

water_use.notes: See PARAMETERS.md (case root). Adult shrub water use with substantial structural wood may differ strongly; treat as a trial proxy.

reproduction.status: AUTHOR trial numbers; qualitative precedent only (FEIS Steinberg 2001: seed production by about age 3 yr, ~131 or 97 pods/tree, ~12 seeds/pod of which ~5 destroyed by bruchids, no seedling emergence from seeds deeper than 5 cm, one-year seedling survival 27% in clipped vs 9.4% in unclipped plots; Texas/other sites, not a per-patch annual establishment probability, so 0.05 stays [AUTHOR]). clonal is null because resprouting is not equivalent to independent ramets. Requires the explicit session reproduction_patch_size_m (5 m in case.toml, case root).

units.establishment_probability: per ecological patch, species and annual opportunity (NOT per hydraulic cell)
units.initial_agb_dry_kg: kg dry aboveground per seedling; an EXTERNAL establishment/seed-reserve credit

reproduction.notes: External-propagule assumption: no seed bank, no dispersal kernel, no water filter. New IDs, age 0, once per annual boundary.

life_expectancy.notes: [AUTHOR] nominal mean age-component lifespan, METADATA ONLY: not an age cutoff. Literature check rev1: FEIS (Steinberg 2001) reports MAXIMUM stand ages of 40-110 years near Amarillo TX and 172-217 years in the Rio Grande Plains, with 89-93% of Rio Grande Plains plants under 100 years; these are maxima/age-structure truncation, not a mean lifespan, so 80 years is not changed to them.

units.biomass_loss_fraction: fraction of B lost by a surviving stressed plant [AUTHOR]

mortality.notes: Weibull scale = 80/0.886226925 = 90.27033336764101. Full model lifespan can be shortened by stress and disturbance. No freezing mortality and no fire.

Abrasion is explicitly disabled (null) until a dose unit and calibrated response exist; sediment flux is never equated with dose. Establishment ground anchor retained; surface-to-soil remapping deferred.
